cluster_00_selected.instructions: Which bounded hypothesis best encloses one distinct visible object or obstacle supported by the structured CV evidence? Choose none when the cluster is clutter, a floor-only interruption, or insufficiently object-like. Select a fused box only when independent detector cues agree on one compact spatial mode. Boxes from one detector are correlated and count as one cue. Do not use a large floor, wall, image-border, or edge region as object support, and do not combine separated object-sized modes with a union or median. A single compact, high-confidence raw proposal may be usable when it is isolated and not contradicted by broad cues. A compact closed-edge rectangle with plausible image geometry may remain usable even when its edge confidence is lower than a color-region confidence. When a weighted_median, union, or intersection hypothesis is supported by at least two independent detector names and is close to a raw fragment, prefer that multi-detector consensus over a single-detector partial box; do not let one high-confidence fragment beat a compact object-sized consensus.
